description: What the repository being changed can be asked about the order its work must happen in, and what it cannot.
why: policies/coupling-policy.json says file disjointness is necessary and not sufficient, and then only implements the sufficient half: named surfaces that two roles must not both edit. The necessary half was missing. Two tasks editing the same file, or one editing a module the other imports, are ordered whether or not anyone named a surface for it.

The alternative to deriving this is asking a proposer to know it, and a proposer reasoning about a repository it has not read will produce an ordering that sounds right. The repository already contains the answer.

signals.means: Two tasks declare paths that intersect.
signals.why: Not an inference. Two agents editing one file in parallel produce a conflict or a lost edit, whichever the merge notices.
signals.edge: sequence them in declared order; the second waits

signals.means: A file one task owns imports a file another task owns.
signals.why: The importer is written against the imported thing. Changing both at once means writing against something that is moving.
signals.edge: the importing task waits for the imported one

signals.means: Two tasks own files that this repository's own history changes together, at or above the threshold.
signals.why: A static scan cannot see a coupling expressed through configuration, dependency injection, a message name or a database column. The history can: files that keep changing together are coupled by something, even when nothing imports anything.

co_change.why: Three commits and half the time, so a pair that moved together twice by coincidence is not evidence. A pair over the threshold is reported for a human or a proposer to judge, because history says these move together and not why.

import_patterns.why: A regex is not a parser. These find the common, static, literal form of an import in each language and nothing else. A project adds its own here rather than editing the script.

cannot_see: Dynamic imports, reflection, dependency injection and service locators. The edge exists at runtime and appears nowhere a regex can read.
Coupling through data: a shared table, a column, a queue name, a feature flag. CS-03 is the only signal that catches any of this, and it catches it as a correlation.
Re-exports and barrel files. A imports B which re-exports C; the edge to C is invisible.
Generated code, vendored code and anything not in the working tree.
Any language with no entry in import_patterns. An unlisted extension yields no import signal, and the run says which extensions it skipped rather than reporting a clean scan.
never: Remove an edge. Inference adds ordering; it does not decide that ordering is unnecessary.
Add an edge that would make the graph cyclic. A cycle means the split was wrong, and that is a refusal, not something to resolve by dropping one of the two edges.
Add a CS-03 edge. History is evidence that two things move together, not a statement about which must land first.
